analysis.title: The Ballot and the Bull
key_insights: The S&P 500 has been higher 12 months after the election-day close following every midterm from 1946 to 2022 (20 of 20), with an average gain of +14.4% and a median of +13.7%.
Since 1930 the S&P 500 was higher 12 months after 22 of 24 midterms (92%), with an average gain of +13.0% and a median of +13.7%.

A post-midterm year has beaten a typical year by roughly 4-5 percentage points on average and about 2 points at the median. Calendar years since 1928 are up 67% of the time, averaging +8.1% with a median of +11.6%. Since 1946 they are up 71% of the time, averaging +9.1% with a median of +11.6%. All figures are price returns excluding dividends.
The midterm year is usually the weakest part of the four-year cycle because political and policy uncertainty peaks before the vote. In the average midterm path the low comes at the end of September.
2026 has not seen the falls of many earlier midterm years, but the market has been flat since the end of May, which DB reads as the usual pre-vote softness.
The election removes uncertainty, and the usual result is divided government and gridlock, which lowers the risk of major policy changes.

The two exceptions were 1930 (-37% over the next 12 months, Great Depression, banking failures, deflation, Smoot-Hawley tariffs) and 1938 (-5.1%, end of the 1937-38 recession). 1946 was an almost-miss at +0.1%.

DB's overall view is that the broad market and most individual stocks are likely to be higher in 12 months, with median and average gains in double digits. Whether the run reaches a 22nd consecutive positive post-midterm period depends on a handful of mega-cap stocks.

The main risks are index concentration, which is higher than in any historical example, and Fed hiking pricing. The market is pricing the mildest hiking cycle in history, and a more normal cycle would likely shock markets.

tension_points.bull_case: The S&P 500 was higher 12 months after every midterm from 1946 to 2022 (20 of 20), averaging +14.4%. The election removes uncertainty and tends to produce gridlock.
tension_points.bear_case: The index is more concentrated than in any historical example, so a few mega-cap disappointments could break the record. The market also prices the mildest hiking cycle in history, and a normal cycle would be a shock.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A few mega-cap companies disappointing, or the Fed hiking more than the market prices.
